title: Metronome Rollout Regulator: cadence-driven canary control with automatic dampening and shadow probes
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Implement a flexible, cadence-driven canary policy engine (the 'Metronome') that controls traffic splits, step schedules, and guardrails for model rollouts. Unlike static step schedulers, Metronome adjusts progression tempo based on real-time metric velocity, supports shadow probing and A/B cohort assignments, and exposes explicit fail-open/fail-closed semantics for private and dedicated deployments.
motivation: Current canary controllers use fixed step durations and simple threshold checks which lead to either slow rollouts or higher risk of regressions. Metronome aims to balance speed with safety by using metric derivatives, dampening rules to avoid oscillation, and shadow probes to validate behavior before traffic escalation.
design_decisions: Cadence model: rollout defined as sequence of beats (time windows) rather than absolute percentages. Each beat contains target split and minimum observation window.
Velocity gating: progression requires both absolute metric thresholds and rate-of-change stability for two consecutive beats.
Dampening: if metric variance exceeds configured band, reduce progression step size by configured factor (e.g., halving step increments).
Shadow probing: lightweight percentage of traffic duplicated to candidate model in shadow mode with tagged telemetry to compare distributions without impacting users.
Cohort sampling: cohort keys support sticky assignment for A/B and can specify stratified sampling by region, customer tier, or token length buckets.
Rollback: automatic rollback triggers include composite rules (latency p99 uplift + error-rate spike OR user-defined eval regression). Manual rollback remains possible from Console with audit log.
Compatibility: policy expressed as YAML-compatible spec persisted in config store and referenced by route. Backwards compatibility adapter translates simple step lists to Metronome beats.
Security: rollout control plane actions audited; private deployments must opt into auto-rollback via enterprise policy flag.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (spike): implement core scheduler and beat lifecycle with static beats and basic metric checks (2 sprints).
Phase 2 (velocity gating): add derivative-based progression and dampening rules; integrate with runtime telemetry streams (1 sprint).
Phase 3 (shadow probes & cohorts): add shadow duplication path, cohort stratification, and sticky assignment; simulate in dev cluster (2 sprints).
Phase 4 (Console + rollout UI): surface beat timelines, per-beat metrics, and one-click rollback in Redwood Console (1 sprint).
Phase 5 (hardening): run canary chaos experiments, runbook, and performance regression tests ahead of runtime-1.20 GA (1 sprint).
canary_policy_spec: top-level keys: name, description, beats[], metrics[], cohorts[], shadow_config, rollback_rules, routing_policy
beat schema: {id, target_percent, min_duration_seconds, min_requests, required_stability_beats, dampening_factor_override}
metrics: supports p50/p95/p99 latency, error_rate, model-quality-eval (custom eval score), and custom counters. Each metric entry supports absolute thresholds and derivative thresholds.
cohorts: named cohorts with sampling_ratio and matching_rules (region, customer_tier, request_signature).
rollback_rules: rule expressions combining metric predicates and time windows. Example: (p99_latency > 1200ms AND delta(p99_latency,60s) > 200ms) OR (error_rate > 0.02).
routing_policy: 'strict' | 'graceful' | 'probabilistic' with explicit fallback model list and priority ordering.
metrics_and_alerts: Default watchlist: p99 latency, request error rate (5xx+prediction failures), model-eval drift score, token_loss_rate (when available).
Progression condition: each beat requires metric stability for required_stability_beats. Stability defined as stddev(metric) < configured_band AND derivative magnitude < derivative_threshold.
Auto-pause: if any metric violates an emergency threshold, the Metronome pauses progression and opens a 'quarantine window' for diagnostics (default 10 minutes).
Alerting: send to #rollouts slack channel, create incident ticket if emergency threshold crossed; create Event in Console timeline with suggested actions.
experiments: Shadow probe A: mirror 2% of production traffic for 24h to candidate model and compare n-gram distribution & latency percentiles.
Metronome vs fixed-step A/B: run parallel canaries on two internal routes to measure time-to-100% while keeping incident rate < 0.5x baseline.
Cohort sensitivity test: release to 5% of enterprise customers in us-west first; compare metrics vs randomized cohort to validate stratified sampling benefits.
implementation_notes: Core scheduler implemented as a controller in the control plane with idempotent beat state machine persisted in config-store (etcd/managed DB).
Telemetry integration: use existing runtime exporters; implement lightweight aggregation layer to compute derivatives and variance over sliding windows with bounded memory.
Shadow duplication: implement sampling upstream in ingress proxy to avoid extra routing hops; ensure side-effect protection option is respected for write-heavy endpoints.
Rollout API: expose REST + SDK hooks to submit policy, query state, and force pause/rollback. Ensure RBAC checks for private deployments.
Testing harness: add simulator that can replay historical traffic and inject metric anomalies to validate dampening and rollback heuristics.
testing_plan: Unit tests for beat state transitions and rollback rule parser.
Integration tests using synthetic traffic generator replaying 7 days of production traffic with injected anomalies.
Chaos test: randomly drop metrics or delay telemetry to ensure Metronome errs safe and pauses progression.
End-to-end: perform internal canary on staging with shadow probes active and validate Console UX shows per-beat metric deltas.
open_questions: What is the canonical derivation and sliding window for derivative calculations (30s vs 60s)?
Should private deployment default to auto-rollback off or opt-in? Current plan: opt-in via enterprise flag.
How to surface multi-metric tradeoffs in Console when metrics disagree (latency improves but eval score drops)?
Do we support non-time-based beats (e.g., proceed after X successful predictions) as first-class behavior?
next_steps: Finalize metric derivative spec and default bands (engineering RFC due 2026-02-18).
Prototype beat state machine and run simulator against archived traces (P0).
Design Console mockups for beat timeline and emergency pause flow (with Design lead by 2026-02-28).
Schedule security review for private deployment auto-rollback behavior (owner: Jordan Blake).
